entry.title: After booting 760K off ACA health plans, the Trump administration adds some people back
entry.summary: The Trump administration provided few details about its process for canceling hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act enrollments — even as the next stage of the anti-fraud effort is underway.

entry.title: Essential items to stock in your medicine cabinet for cold and flu season
entry.summary: Cold and flu season is here. Before someone in your household gets hit, make sure you have these essential meds and comfort items in your medicine cabinet.

entry.title: These workers help train robots who could one day steal their jobs
entry.summary: Factory workers in India are being asked to wear GoPro cameras to record the way they do their jobs. The ultimate goal is to train robots to take over. Will it work?

entry.title: VIDEO: The skincare sample is free. What happens next can cost thousands
entry.summary: For years, customers have complained of aggressive sales tactics and charges at mall skincare stores. NPR investigated the business that connects many of them.

entry.title: What to know about Pope Leo's lung cancer diagnosis
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks to Dr. Otis Brawley, an oncologist at Johns Hopkins University, about the Pope's lung cancer diagnosis.

entry.title: Writer Yiyun Li lost both of her sons. When words fell short, she turned to music
entry.summary: Li won a Pulitzer for her memoir about the suicides of her two sons. In her new novel, Music Against the Night, she writes about two young prodigies in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

entry.title: Sauna research gathers steam
entry.summary: Leading researchers in heat exposure are coming together to reach a consensus on what we know — and don't — about the health benefits of sauna and its potential for treating and preventing disease.

entry.title: Here's what to know if you're unsure about your measles immunity status
entry.summary: Vaccination is the best way to protect yourself against measles. For most adults, one shot of the MMR is considered enough protection. But there are certain situations that call for a second dose.

entry.title: How one antibiotic morning-after pill came to be widely available in San Francisco
entry.summary: An antibiotic morning-after pill has been shown to be effective for preventing STIs among gay men, but some doctors worry about antibiotic resistance. This story discusses STIs and their symptoms.

entry.title: Don't be scared: Being afraid is outright fun, and maybe useful
entry.summary: Listeners of NPR's Weekend Edition Sunday may already know that host Ayesha Rascoe loves horror. But why do scream queens (and kings) like her like what's frightening? The answer may surprise you.
